thread:
linda-cs: Flagging Harvest onboarding: usage spike after integration tests — cost is ~1.25x forecast and interactive p95 creeping to ~420ms. Renewal touchpoint in three weeks. Looking for quick, low-risk perf knobs we can propose (quant, model swap, routing, prompt edits). Any short checklist?

tom-eng: Short list from infra side: 1) route heavy parallel inference (bulk annotation/rerank) to a dedicated pool during nightly windows; 2) enable short-sequence batching for chat; 3) toggle smaller model for low-priority routes.

yasmin-ml: From quality POV, two ideas: distilled variant (redwood-lite-1) reduces token-cost ~30% on short convs but fails on multi-turn stateful code prompts. Alternative is q4_8bit on production but only for routes that match a short-length predicate.

kevin-ops: Operational constraints: Harvest wants no customer-visible content changes without sign-off. So prefer routing + canary-first approach. Also we can apply prefix caching for their top 15 repeated system prompts; that's often low-risk.

linda-cs: Client will accept canaries if we provide clear rollback criteria and a short enablement call. Proposed fallback: 24-hour canary, escalate if quality delta > 1.5% or error rate > 3x baseline.

yasmin-ml: Canary suggestion: start with 5% -> 25% -> 75% over 3 days with automatic checks at each step. Exclude routes flagged as `sessionized-code`. Sample canary config (pseudo):
```
route: harvest.chat.prod
steps:
  - percent: 5
    duration: 24h
  - percent: 25
    duration: 24h
  - percent: 75
    duration: 24h
variant_map:
  control: redwood-base-fp16
  candidate: redwood-lite-1 (or q4_8bit for non-code)
exclude_tags: ["codegen","sessionized-code"]
checks:
  - metric: quality-diff
    eval_set: harvest-smoke-v2
    threshold: -0.015
  - metric: p95-latency
    threshold: -0.10 (expect improvement)
```
Note: we should use both a distilled candidate and a quantized candidate in parallel canaries on separate routes to compare cost/quality tradeoffs.

tom-eng: I'll add token-level cost feed into the CS health dashboard and create a rollback runbook. Also recommend enforcing client-side prompt truncation for >512 tokens and adding an opt-in compress middleware for their SDK to reduce repeated context.

linda-cs: For customer comms: short note + KPIs (latency, cost delta, perceived quality). I'll ask for permission to run the canary for low-volume traffic first.

kevin-ops: I'll provision a small dedicated pool for house-keeping and nightly reranks to pull load off the shared host. Also setting up KV cache for the top templates.

orion-bot: Created task CS-7812: Harvest canary planning. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-7812. Owners: yasmin-ml, tom-eng, linda-cs.

yasmin-ml: One caution: if we use q4 on the main route, watch tokenization artifacts on long entity-heavy strings. I can roll a tiny tokenizer patch to normalise some of their IDs; low risk and often improves q4 quality.

linda-cs: OK plan summary: 1) run 48h 5% distilled canary + parallel 5% q4 on non-code routes, 2) enable prompt-template KV caching, 3) route batch jobs to dedicated pool nights, 4) measure cost delta and p95 and report. I will log this in renewal board (status: being-trialed). Scheduling 20m enablement with Harvest for tomorrow.

tom-eng: 👍 will push dashboard widgets and the canary toggle.

kevin-ops: Sending calendar invite and pre-read now.

linda-cs: Thanks team — will capture Harvest feedback in Gainsight and attach example diffs.
